text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Party leaders, campaigning for the parliamentary elections, sharpen rhetoric with threat to pull out of the race or unveil files on their opponents' behaviour.
- Security forces kill 134 gunmen in operations in western Algeria. Two civilians killed by "terrorists" at a road in northern Algeria.
- A home-made bomb explosion wounds five people in Draa Ben Khedda town, in the northeastern province of Tizi-Ouzou.
- The 1,200 km (700 mile) highway linking the eastern town of Constantine to the western city of Oran needs 15 billion dinars (about $300 million) financing.
- Islamist Mahfoud Nahnah, leader of the Movement for a Peaceful Society, threatens to withdraw from the poll to protest at what he called mud-slinging campaign by his foes.
- Hassen Laskri, a government minister contending for a seat in the upcoming parliament, says his National Democratic Rally party wants peace and restored order in the country.
- The "war of words" has started: party leaders trade bitter criticism, dodging true debates on voter concerns.
- Algeria aims to double its current 30 billion cubic metres gas exports by year 2000.
- Eldery people were forgotten by political parties compaigning for the elections. There is no word about their situation in the party platforms.
- Government rewards for tips leading to the capture or killing of "terrorists" begin yielding results with several "terrorists" killed by security forces.
